get.summary: Get the current API key user
Serve a signed v1 evidence frame

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: Storage key of the frame, exactly as in the signed URL: `frames/…` for spaces scanned with the app, `api/…` for scans made through the API.

get.summary: List the spaces this key can read: scanned with the app (live keys) and created through the API

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Only spaces from this source. Omitted: every space this key can read (app spaces need a live key; test keys see the demo space).

post.summary: Create a space to scan through the API
post.description: Creates a space in the key's mode (test or live). With an `external_id` already used in that mode, returns the existing space with 200 instead of creating another. An account creates at most 200 spaces a day in each mode (by default, test keys included; a replay does not count): past that, 429 `RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` with `Retry-After` (seconds to midnight UTC). Needs `spaces:read` and `scans:write`.

get.summary: Get the current document for a space
get.description: Keys without the `spaces:sensitive` scope only read what the deep pass has screened for sensitive values. Until it has (`enrichment.level` is `base`), the document has the same shape with its content withheld: the lists are empty and `stats` gives the counts. Once `enrichment.level` is `deep`, sensitive facts are redacted, their values are removed from every other text, and images are given only for the frames that non-sensitive records cite as evidence. Fields the deep pass does not read (project description, summary, area layout) and raw first-hand sources (transcript, owner answers, narrator quotes) always require the scope.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: Adds the transcript. Requires the `spaces:sensitive` scope; without it the request is refused with 403 `INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE`.

delete.summary: Delete a space created through the API, with its scans and files
delete.description: Not possible while one of its scans is processing (409). App spaces are deleted in the app. Needs `scans:write`.

post.summary: Create a scan of a space created through the API
post.description: Declares what will be uploaded (frames with their timestamps, or one video), the language and the optional transcript. The response says how to upload in `upload`; then call `POST /scans/{id}/start`. The same `Idempotency-Key` returns the same scan. An account creates at most 500 scans a day in each mode (by default, test keys included; a replay does not count): past that, 429 `RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` with `Retry-After` (seconds to midnight UTC). Needs `scans:write`.

200.description: The scan created with this Idempotency-Key

get.summary: Get a base document for a specific scan
get.description: A scan read by id is the snapshot as it was recorded. Past scans are not screened for sensitive values, so this operation requires the `spaces:sensitive` scope and answers 403 `INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE` without it.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: Adds the transcript. Requires the `spaces:sensitive` scope; without it the request is refused with 403 `INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE`.

get.summary: Export a space as a multi-file Agent Skill
get.description: Returns the files of a ready-to-use skill built from the current document, exactly as this key may read it: a redacted document gives a redacted skill. `SKILL.md` is a short static guide; the knowledge is in `references/` and `space.json`, which an agent opens only when needed. A key without `spaces:sensitive` gets 409 `ENRICHMENT_PENDING` until the deep pass has screened the analysis.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: Adds `references/transcript.md`. Requires the `spaces:sensitive` scope; without it the request is refused with 403 `INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE`.

get.summary: Export a space as one Markdown page
get.description: The current document as a single readable page (`text/markdown`): summary, every area with its items, issues, key locations and how-to steps, then facts, Q&A, coverage and the recording. Built from exactly the document this key may read, so a redacted document gives a redacted page; image links are never included. The same 409 `ENRICHMENT_PENDING` rule as the Skill export applies to keys without `spaces:sensitive`.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: Adds the transcript. Requires the `spaces:sensitive` scope; without it the request is refused with 403 `INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE`.

post.summary: Ask a question about a space
post.description: Answers from the records of the current document this key may read, in one to three sentences, with the records it relies on and their evidence images. Says so when the answer is not documented, and never reveals a redacted value. Test keys get the best-matching record of the demo, without a model. A key without `spaces:sensitive` gets 409 `ENRICHMENT_PENDING` until the space is screened. Limits: 20 a minute and, by default, 200 a day per account.

get.summary: Compare two scans of a space
get.description: What changed from the scan `from` to the scan `to` (the current one when omitted): areas, items added, removed, not seen, moved or changed, issues new, resolved or not seen. Computed without a model. When `to` was checked against `from` (consecutive scans of a space created through the API) records are matched by the links it made, and removals are confirmed by a frame of the empty place; otherwise records are matched by content (name, generic name, aliases) and what is missing is reported as `not_seen`. For a space scanned with the app, past scans are not screened for sensitive values, so this operation requires the `spaces:sensitive` scope.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Id of the later scan. Defaults to the current one.

get.description: Finds the records (items, areas, issues, key locations, instructions, facts, questions and answers) that best match a question in natural language, across every space this key can read, in any of 100+ languages: "where did I see a ladder?". Each result names its space, scan and record, so it can be opened with the other operations. The index holds only screened, redacted content: no result ever contains a sensitive value, whatever the key's scopes. A space appears once its current scan has been indexed: after a scan completes, or after the deep pass of a space scanned with the app. Test keys search the demo space, without a model. Limits: 20 a minute and, by default, 1000 a day per account.

get.summary: What this key has to spend
get.description: For agents: the balance, the free scans left, the price of a scan and whether a card is on file (`card_on_file`: live scans need one). Needs the `scans:read` scope.
Poll until `status` is `complete` or `failed`. A failed scan costs nothing: it is charged at start and refunded on failure, and `charge.refunded` says so. Needs `scans:read`.

delete.summary: Cancel a scan that has not started
delete.description: Nothing was charged; its uploads are deleted. Needs `scans:write`.

get.summary: Follow a scan in real time
get.description: A `text/event-stream` (Server-Sent Events) that sends the scan (the same object as `GET /scans/{id}`, without `upload`) as an event named `scan` at once, then every time its status, stage or error changes, and closes after the final one (`complete`, `failed` or `cancelled`). A `ping` event every 15 seconds keeps the connection alive. One stream lasts at most 30 minutes; reconnect to keep following. An account holds at most 10 streams open at once (by default): one more answers 429 with `Retry-After`; close one, or poll `GET /scans/{id}`. Needs `scans:read`.

200.description: Event stream: `event: scan` with the scan as JSON data; `event: ping` with no data.

put.summary: Upload one frame of a frames scan
put.description: The raw image as the body: JPEG, PNG or WebP (recognised by its bytes), at most 2 MB. Sending a frame again replaces it. Needs `scans:write`.

put.summary: Upload the video of a video scan through the API
put.description: Only when `upload.url` points here (no direct upload link available). `Content-Length` and `Content-Type` must match what was declared. Needs `scans:write`.

post.summary: Charge the scan and start the analysis
post.description: Checks that every frame (or the video) is uploaded, uses the free scan or charges the wallet, and starts the analysis. Answers 202 when it started the scan and 200 when the scan had already started. A failed analysis is refunded. Errors: 402 `PAYMENT_METHOD_REQUIRED` (a live scan needs a card on file: added in the console, nothing charged), `INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS` or `SPENDING_CAP_REACHED`, 409 `UPLOAD_INCOMPLETE`, 429 `SCANS_IN_PROGRESS`, 503 `PAYMENTS_UNAVAILABLE` (a live scan where payments are not configured). Test keys are never charged and get the demo result. Needs `scans:write`.

For apps that capture a space: is this frame usable, and which key locations (electrical_panel, water_shutoff, water_heater, smoke_detector, fire_extinguisher, router, heating_control, gas_meter) does it show. The raw image as the body: JPEG, PNG or WebP, at most 2 MB. About half a second; nothing is stored. Free within a daily allowance per account (429 when used up). Test keys get a fixed answer. Needs `scans:write`. Errors: 415 `INVALID_CONTENT_TYPE`, 503 `FRAME_CHECK_UNAVAILABLE`.

A terminal that has no browser session asks for a code. It shows `user_code` and `verification_url` to the person, who opens the console and types the code (never a link with the code in it: a link could be sent by someone else to get their terminal approved), then polls `POST /auth/device/token` with `device_code` every `interval` seconds. The code lives `expires_in` seconds. Public; limited per IP.

201.description: Codes for the terminal and the person

post.description: Answers 400 `AUTHORIZATION_PENDING` until the person decides, 400 `SLOW_DOWN` when polled faster than `interval`, 400 `DEVICE_CODE_EXPIRED` after ten minutes, 403 `ACCESS_DENIED` when denied, and the new API key exactly once when approved. Public.

post.summary: Pay with x402 and get an API key (agents)
post.description:
For an agent with a wallet and no account: pay in USDC on **Base** or **Solana** with [x402](https://x402.org) v2 and receive an API key. No key, no sign-in: the payment is the credential, and the paying address is the account. Any x402 v2 client works (for example `@x402/fetch` with `@x402/evm` and `@x402/svm`): the network fee is paid by the facilitator, the payer needs only USDC.

1. Call without `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE`: 402 `PAYMENT_REQUIRED` with the `PAYMENT-REQUIRED` header (base64 JSON, also in the body as `payment_required`). `accepts` has one entry per network, Base first: scheme `exact`, the network (CAIP-2), the amount in atomic USDC units (6 decimals: US$1.00 = `1000000`), the USDC contract or mint, the address to pay, and `extra` (the EIP-712 domain of USDC on Base; on Solana `feePayer`, the facilitator account that pays the network fee). `extensions.bazaar` describes the call for x402 catalogs.
2. Pick one entry, sign it, and send **the same request, with the same body**, adding `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE` (base64 JSON PaymentPayload with that entry, unchanged, as `accepted`). On Base the payload is an EIP-3009 `transferWithAuthorization`; on Solana a transaction partially signed by the payer: SetComputeUnitLimit, SetComputeUnitPrice, a `TransferChecked` of exactly the amount into the USDC account of `payTo`, optional memo, fee payer `extra.feePayer`. The payment is verified and settled by the facilitator; the answer carries `PAYMENT-RESPONSE` with the transaction.

On mainnet (Base `eip155:8453`, Solana `solana:5eykt4UsFv8P8NJdTREpY1vzqKqZKvdp`) the payment is credited to the account's wallet (`amount_cents`, then US$1.00 per live scan; reading, search and answers are included; agents have no free scan; the credit does not expire) and the key is **live**. On testnets (Base Sepolia `eip155:84532`, Solana devnet `solana:EtWTRABZaYq6iMfeYKouRu166VU2xqa1`) USDC is free, so the payment credits nothing: the key is a **test** key (demo space, no charges, no model). The same paying address always gets the same account; a Base wallet and a Solana wallet are two accounts.

**Store `api_key` from your first purchase: it is shown once.** A signed authorization can be submitted by whoever holds it, so a payment alone returns a key only when it opens the account. Later payments from the same wallet top up the same account and return only `api_key_prefix`. An existing key is replaced only with that key: `rotate_key: true` plus `Authorization: Bearer <the current key>` (the previous key is revoked). The first key of the other mode (e.g. a live key for an account that so far paid on testnet) needs `Authorization: Bearer <one of the account's current keys>`. Both are checked before any payment is taken (403 `AGENT_KEY_REQUIRED`, nothing charged). A payment replayed with the same transaction is recognised: nothing is credited or minted twice.

400 `PAYMENT_INVALID` when the signature header is malformed or does not match the requirements (amount, network, asset, address, fee payer, the payer's signature), before anything is sent to the facilitator. 402 `PAYMENT_FAILED` when the facilitator rejects or cannot settle the payment (`reason`; nothing was charged). 503 `PAYMENTS_UNAVAILABLE` when the chosen network cannot be served right now (nothing was charged). 404 when agent payments are off on this deployment. Limited per IP.

parameters.name: PAYMENT-SIGNATURE
parameters.description: base64 of the JSON x402 v2 PaymentPayload: `x402Version: 2`, `accepted` (one entry of `accepts`, unchanged), and `payload`: on Base `{ signature, authorization: { from, to, value, validAfter, validBefore, nonce } }`, on Solana `{ transaction }` (base64 of the partially signed transaction).

200.description: Paid: the account, its credit (mainnet) and its key

PAYMENT-RESPONSE.description: base64 of the JSON settlement: `{ success, transaction, network, payer }`

402.description: `PAYMENT_REQUIRED` (pay first) or `PAYMENT_FAILED` (rejected or not settled; nothing was charged)

PAYMENT-RESPONSE.description: On `PAYMENT_FAILED`: base64 of `{ success: false, errorReason, payer, transaction, network }`

403.description: `AGENT_KEY_REQUIRED`: changing the keys of an existing account needs one of its current keys (nothing was charged)

500.description: Settled but not recorded: reconciled by hand (`transaction`)

502.description: The settlement could not be confirmed (`nonce` on Base, `signature` on Solana)

RateLimited.description: Too many requests. Retry after the number of seconds in `Retry-After`.

Items and issues seen again carry `previous_item_id` / `previous_issue_id`; what is gone is listed only when a frame of this scan shows the place where it was. card_on_file.description: A real card stands behind the account: a card saved in the console, a paid top-up, or a settled x402 payment on mainnet. Starting a live scan, and creating a live key that can scan, need it: without it they answer 402 `PAYMENT_METHOD_REQUIRED`. Adding a card charges nothing.

tax_added.description: Whether tax is added on top of top-ups and automatic recharges where it applies (such as VAT), from the billing address and tax ID, and shown on the payment page and the invoice. A business with a valid VAT number in another EU country is invoiced under the reverse charge. The balance always receives the amount before tax.

terms_accepted.description: Console only (absent from `GET /wallet`): the first time this account accepted the current version of the billing terms, with the box of a payment or card page; null if never, or only an older version. The box is still ticked on every page (`accept_terms`), and the first acceptance is kept on later payments for a dispute.

headers.description: Headers the PUT must carry. Content-Length must equal the declared size (HTTP clients set it from the body).

usable.description: Sharp, lit and showing a place: worth keeping in a scan.

shows_space.description: Probability that the frame shows a real place (not a drawing, document or screen).

seen.description: At least one frame shows it (probability from 0.7).

probability.description: The highest probability over the frames.

name.description: What is asking, shown to the person: "CLI on MacBook". Default "CLI".

mode.description: The mode of the key asked for (the person can change it). Default live.

device_code.description: The terminal's secret: never shown to the person.

verification_url.description: The console page where the person types the code.

api_key.description: The new key: shown once, store it.

amount_cents.description: US cents to pay (and, on mainnet, to credit): US$1.00 is one live scan. x402 clients cap a payment at US$1 by default; raise their limit to pay more at once

rotate_key.description: Make a new key and revoke the current one. Needs `Authorization: Bearer <the current key>`

payer.description: Lowercase on Base; base58 as written on Solana

livemode.description: true on mainnet: live credit and a live key

balance_cents.description: The wallet after this payment; null on testnet (nothing is credited)

api_key.description: Only when the key was created by this call: store it, it is not shown again

api_key_prefix.description: The account's key of this mode; null when it has none

notice.description: What to do with the key (store it now, or use the one stored)

amount.description: Atomic units of the asset (USDC: 6 decimals)

payTo.description: Who is paid: on Solana, the owner of the USDC account the transfer goes to

anyOf.description: Base: the EIP-712 domain of USDC
Solana: the facilitator account that pays the network fee (the transaction's fee payer)

extensions.description: `bazaar`: how to call this resource and what it returns, for x402 catalogs

reason.description: Why the payment was refused (x402 reason)

transaction.description: On 500: the settled transaction, for reconciliation

nonce.description: On 502 (Base): the authorization nonce, for reconciliation

signature.description: On 502 (Solana): the payer's transaction signature, for reconciliation

retry_after.description: On a 429: seconds to wait, as in `Retry-After`.

daily_limit.description: On a 429 for a daily allowance: the allowance (it resets at midnight UTC).

max_streams.description: On a 429 from `GET /scans/{id}/events`: the streams an account may hold open at once.
